svg.aria-label: A laptop at home cannot reach the file share because port 445 is blocked. The portal uploads over HTTPS with the storage key. A snapshot keeps Version 1 of policy.txt and a restore brings it back. With Entra, Owner is denied; File Data Privileged Reader can list but not upload. A VM in Azure mounts the share over SMB with the key until shared key access is turned off, which cuts it off while Entra access keeps working.
svg.title: One file share, three ways in
svg.text: One file share, three ways in: who gets through, and with what
az-104-labs · lab 06 Azure Files · SMB vs HTTPS, keys vs Entra roles, snapshots

g.text: 1 From home: SMB on port 445 is blocked before it leaves the building
2 Portal upload over HTTPS (443): works, using the storage key
3 Snapshot taken: policy.txt frozen at Version 1
3 Live file changed to Version 2; the snapshot still says Version 1
3 Restore from the snapshot: Version 1 is back
4 Switch to Entra as Owner: denied, Owner has no data actions
5 Add Storage File Data Privileged Reader: listing works
6 Same Reader role tries to upload: denied, no write
7 VM inside Azure maps the share over SMB with the key: works
8 Shared key access OFF: the VM is cut off, Entra still reads

svg.text: share · Transaction optimized · soft delete 7 days

g.text: written over SMB, seen over HTTPS

svg.text: Port 445: SMB needs outbound 445. Home and many ISP networks block it; HTTPS on 443 is not affected.
Access key: the portal quietly read the key, which an Owner may do. The key opens every share in the account.
Snapshot: a read-only copy of the whole share at one moment. Changes after it never touch it.
Two planes: Owner holds actions, not dataActions. Without the key, it cannot even list the files.
Data role: Storage File Data Privileged Reader is for portal, CLI and REST. SMB uses the SMB Share roles.
Least privilege: Reader lists and downloads. Writing needs Privileged Contributor.
Inside Azure: 445 is open, so SMB works. The SMB username is the account name; the password is the key.
Keys off: every key, SAS and key-based SMB mount stops at once. Only Entra roles over HTTPS remain.
A storage key is one password for every file. Roles say who; keys only say "someone with the key".
Identity-based SMB (per-user mounts) needs AD DS, Entra Domain Services or Entra Kerberos: not set up in this lab.
